sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in the menu bar library, icons, and style helper. Nothing is shown on screen.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets up the parts the menu bar uses.

sections.name: MenubarMenu
sections.title: Single menu pass-through wrapper
sections.what: Passes a single menu through to the menu bar library without changing it.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the menu parts available under this file's names so the rest of the app uses one import.

sections.name: MenubarGroup
sections.title: Group pass-through wrapper
sections.what: Passes a group of menu items through to the library without changing it.
sections.why: Likely reason: same as above, for groups.

sections.name: MenubarPortal
sections.title: Portal pass-through wrapper
sections.what: Passes the portal through to the library without changing it. The portal draws menus above the page.
sections.why: Likely reason: same as above, for the layer that draws menus.

sections.name: MenubarRadioGroup
sections.title: Radio group pass-through wrapper
sections.what: Passes a group of radio options through to the library without changing it.
sections.why: Likely reason: same as above, for radio choices.

sections.name: MenubarSub (part 1)
sections.title: Menu bar container and top buttons
sections.what: Builds the horizontal bar that holds the top menu buttons, and the top buttons themselves. Buttons highlight when focused or open. The submenu trigger is also styled here.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the bar and its top buttons a consistent look.

sections.name: MenubarSub (part 2)
sections.title: Pop-down boxes and items
sections.what: Builds the box that drops down from a top button, with alignment and a gap set by default, and the items inside it. It also styles the box for submenus.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the drop-down look consistent with other menus.
sections.watch_out: The alignment and gap defaults move every pop-down in the bar at once. Some long style strings were cut off in the copy I was given.

sections.name: MenubarSub (part 3)
sections.title: Checkbox and radio menu items
sections.what: Builds the menu rows that can be ticked on or off, and the rows where only one can be chosen at a time. A check mark or dot appears in the left gutter when the row is selected.
sections.why: Likely reason: they wrap ready-made menu pieces from the Radix library and add the app's styling so they match the rest of the app.
sections.watch_out: The checked state comes from the parent through the checked prop, so a parent that never passes it will not control the box.

sections.name: MenubarSub (part 4)
sections.title: Labels, dividers and shortcut text
sections.what: Provides small pieces for menu headings, thin dividing lines, and right-aligned keyboard hints such as a shortcut key.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the usual menu layout.
sections.watch_out: MenubarShortcut sets displayname in lowercase, so the name will not show correctly in developer tools; the library expects displayName.

sections.name: MenubarSub (part 5)
sections.title: Public list of menu parts
sections.what: Lists every menu piece this file offers so other screens can import them by name.
sections.why: Lets the rest of the app import all menu building blocks from one file.
sections.watch_out: Export names must match what other files import; renaming one breaks those files.

summary: Builds a horizontal menu bar, like the File and Edit bar in desktop apps, with pop-down menus, submenus, items, checkboxes, and radio options. Only the first seven of its ten parts were visible to me.
purpose: Gives the app a top-level menu bar with the same look as the rest of the menus.
why: Likely reason: a shared menu bar keeps top menus consistent with the right-click and dropdown menus. The code does not state this directly.
how: It imports the menu bar library, icons, and style helper. It wraps the bar container, its top buttons, its submenu, and its items. It also passes through several base parts such as the menu, group, portal, and radio group without changing them. The visible parts apply styles to the bar, the top buttons, and the pop-down boxes. The rest of the file, which I could not see, is not described here.
inputs: Settings from the screen, such as style overrides, alignment and gap for pop-down menus, indent flags, and standard element settings.
outputs: A menu bar with pop-down menus. Nothing is stored.
risks: Visual changes affect every menu bar in the app. The last three parts of the file were not visible, so I cannot describe their behavior.
debug: If a menu bar does not open, check the screen that renders it and the trigger buttons. If spacing looks off, check the alignment and gap defaults in the pop-down wrapper. Some long style strings were cut off in the copy I was given.
